children: DriveWealth plans to integrate Ripple’s stablecoin, payments and custody technology, initially focusing on European settlement.

Investors can trade US stocks through digital apps at almost any hour, but moving the cash needed to fund those trades still runs into banking cutoffs. A newly announced partnership between DriveWealth and Ripple aims to close that gap using stablecoin infrastructure.

On October 14 the companies set out plans for RLUSD settlement on the XRP Ledger, beginning in Europe with a prospective US expansion. DriveWealth is also integrating Ripple Payments for cross-border funding and exploring Ripple custody and prime-brokerage services. The release describes both integrations and areas still under exploration; it does not mean every customer can already settle in RLUSD.

This is a practical institutional use case. Even with US equity settlement operating at T+1, international transfers can hold up buying power and leave brokers managing cash buffers across markets. Funds that move more quickly could reduce some of that operational drag, though the conversion between stablecoins and bank money still requires reliable counterparties and controls.

DriveWealth supplies brokerage infrastructure to more than 100 partners. If the promised settlement improvements reach production, they could become visible inside familiar investing applications rather than as a standalone crypto product. The test will be whether stablecoin funding makes the end-to-end customer experience measurably better.
